name: North Ridge (West Face)

pitch_detail.notes: Lower west face of the North Ridge.
Tops out to join the North Ridge crest.

descent_text: Descend the North Ridge, also called the North Cleaver, back toward High Camp. This is a walk-off over loose volcanic scree and boulders and is longer than it looks from above, with a real chance of knocking rock onto parties below, so spread out and move quickly through the worst sections. A rock band on the ridge can be downclimbed, and a short rope-assisted step is sometimes used by parties uneasy with the exposure. From High Camp retrace the High Camp Trail and Killen Creek Trail 113 to the trailhead.
approach: Start at the Killen Creek trailhead on FR 2329 north of Takhlakh Lake and follow Killen Creek Trail 113 south for about 3.2 miles through lodgepole forest and meadows to the Pacific Crest Trail junction near 6,100 ft. Cross the PCT onto the High Camp Trail, a rocky boot path that climbs a volcanic spur for about a mile to High Camp on a flat bench near 6,900 ft; the whole carry is roughly four miles and 2,300 ft. Camp here, since water comes only from snowmelt and the site is very exposed to wind. Above camp the trail ends and the way crosses moraines and old lava flows toward the north side of the mountain, so carry navigation for whiteouts. A Cascade Volcano Pass is required above 7,000 ft.
overview: A straightforward snow/ice line up the west face of Mount Adams's North Ridge, a more technical companion route to the standard North Ridge scramble.
beta: A straightforward snow/ice route up to 50°, following the northwest face of the North Ridge. Bring a snow picket, an ice screw, possibly a few thin pins, and two ice tools.
fa: Molenaar, Johnson, Ostro, and Startzell, September 1960
face: West Face of the North Ridge
